source.title: Londonderry Sentinel, 19 May 1949, p. 6 ("County Londonderry: Limavady - seventeen retiring councillors returned unopposed; the members returned unopposed"); Derry Journal, 20 May 1949, p. 5 ("Rural council elections: returns and contests - Limavady"); Derry Journal, 18 May 1955, p. 2 ("Limavady Rural Council: full list of nominations")
source.publisher: Londonderry Sentinel (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned unopposed: 'Seventeen of the retiring councillors were returned unopposed on Tuesday, but yesterday, following two withdrawals, there will be only four contests ... The members returned unopposed are: ...' (Londonderry Sentinel 19 May 1949 p6, image OCR read; Derry Journal 20 May 1949). The list gives names and townlands, not divisions.

note: Triennial election of the 23 electoral divisions of Limavady rural district, one member each, polled on 2 June 1949. Six contests were nominated, but withdrawals reduced these to four. The Unionists regained control, taking Drumraighland on a drawn lot after a tie. Sixteen of the nineteen unopposed members added from the nominations reports (Londonderry Sentinel, 19 May 1949, p. 6; Derry Journal, 20 May 1949), which name them without divisions: Foreglen and Scriggan from the withdrawals the reports describe, the other fourteen from their divisions at the 1946 return. Aghanloo, Feeny and The Highlands are held: their members (W. J. Thompson, James O'Kane and John Alcorn) are not in the 1946 return, and only later sources place them (round-2 gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). division inferred from the 31 October 1946 return (Con Askin for Faughanvale; Londonderry Sentinel, 2 November 1946, p. 5); the Londonderry Sentinel of 19 May 1949, p. 6, names the member as returned unopposed, a retiring councillor. The 1955 nominations list (Derry Journal, 18 May 1955, p. 2) again names him for this division as its retiring member. Returned unopposed.
